title: Equal work, equal pay
body: I guess Lim Guan Eng, the former finance minister and now adviser to the Democratic Action Party (DAP), has a soft spot for employers. His call to exclude migrant workers from the minimum wage and the paltry 2% contribution to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) repeats a position he took in early August 2025. Even then, labour groups criticised it. Since he has chosen to lend his voice to employers, be they micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) or others, it is apt to remind him of three fundamental issues. All people are equal Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution treats everyone as equal and entitles them to equal protection. The courts have noted this. In Ahmad Zahri bin Mirza Abdul Hamid v AIMS Cyberjaya Sdn Bhd, the Federal Court took cognisance of Article 10 of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention 143 of 1975. It said Malaysia should promote and guarantee equality of opportunity and treatment between migrant workers and nationals. Referring to the convention, the court said: - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Based on the above reasons we take the view that all workers should be treated with fairness, dignity and equality without distinction whether they are locals or foreigners. This is also consonant with Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution which essentially provides that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law. his judgment alone should put to rest the flawed argument that Malaysia should adopt discriminatory standards against migrant workers to protect employers. Legislative protection Section 69F of the Employment Act 1955 empowers the director general of labour to inquire into and decide any dispute over discrimination in employment. An employer who fails to comply with the director general’s order faces, on conviction, a fine of up to RM50,000. For a continuing offence, there is a further fine of up to RM1,000 for each day it continues. Where an employer has signed a collective agreement with a trade union, section 17(1)(b) of the Industrial Relations Act 1967 makes it binding once the Industrial Court takes cognisance of it. It covers all worker employed in the undertaking, now or later. Industrial Court and other judicial decisions have affirmed that such agreements apply to migrant workers. International standards From the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, one fact stands unchallenged – there is no room for discriminatory employment practices against migrant workers. Full stop! No reasonable person would dispute that people doing the same work must receive the same pay. The right to equal pay for equal work should never be compromised. Doing so would destroy the foundation of equality, good conscience and fair treatment of workers, whether migrant or local. Working people need greater protection against the ever-rising cost of living, low and stagnant wages and inadequate retirement savings in the EPF. They do not need more protection for employers. Seeking such protection for employers is like asking workers to wallow in a vicious low-wage ecosystem so that employers can profit from staying in business. To even entertain the thought that businesses should be protected by treating migrant workers as second-class employees is heartless, an affront to human dignity and devoid of any sense of justice. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction
body: PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker. The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions. The transaction enhances transparency and price discovery by making funding levels and spreads visible to a broader network of market participants. This contrasts with bilateral transactions, where pricing information is limited to the counterparties involved. By helping establish a transparent Malaysia Overnight Rate (MYOR) funding curve and an observable reference point for three-month interbank funding, the transaction improves visibility into funding spreads over MYOR and banks’ cost of borrowing, supporting more efficient pricing across the wider market. UOB Malayia corporate and investment banking country head Christina Cheah said, “The successful execution of this money market transaction reflects the strong collaboration between UOB Malaysia, RHB and Maybank in supporting the evolution of the country’s financial markets. By establishing a transparent benchmark for MYOR-based funding, we are contributing to greater price discovery and helping to build confidence in the adoption of risk-free rate conventions. “As a leading foreign bank in the country, UOB Malaysia remains committed to partnering local market participants, sharing regional expertise and supporting initiatives that strengthen market resilience and align the domestic financial ecosystem with global standards.” The transaction references MYOR compounded in arrears with a two-day lookback mechanism, providing operational certainty in interest calculations while remaining anchored to actual market transactions. RHB Banking Group wholesale banking managing director Nurjesmi Mohd Nashir said, “This transaction demonstrates how market participants can work together to put MYOR-based conventions into practice and support the continued development of Malaysia’s money market. “As the industry progresses towards the transition from KLIBOR to MYOR, it is important that we build practical market experience and develop conventions that can be adopted more widely. RHB is committed to supporting Bank Negara Malaysia’s efforts to develop a deeper and more efficient MYOR market, and to playing an active role in the continued development of Malaysia’s financial markets.” Farid Kairi, deputy group CEO of global banking and managing director of global markets said: “Maybank is pleased to have played an integral role in this inaugural MYOR-based money market transaction. It marks an important first step in establishing the foundation for deeper liquidity, while setting the stage for widening the aperture for more MYOR-linked solutions and supporting robust price discovery for market participants. “This achievement reflects the collective efforts of industry participants and Bank Negara Malaysia in strengthening Malaysia’s financial market infrastructure.” Bank Negara Malaysia introduced MYOR in September 2021 as Malaysia’s Alternative Reference Rate (ARR). MYOR is calculated as the volume-weighted average rate of actual unsecured overnight ringgit interbank transactions, providing a robust benchmark grounded in deep and liquid overnight funding markets. The transition towards MYOR aligns Malaysia with other major financial markets that have adopted overnight risk-free rates including Singapore, Japan, Switzerland, the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: EU-Malaysia trade deal: Jangan jejaskan produk perubatan mampu milik dan hak petani / Don’t put affordable medicines, farmers’ rights at risk
body: [ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Persatuan Pengguna Pulau Pinang (CAP) dan 40 pertubuhan masyarakat sivil Malaysia yang lain menggesa kerajaan Malaysia supaya menolak tuntutan hak harta intelek oleh Kesatuan Eropah (EU) yang melangkaui kewajipan Malaysia di bawah Perjanjian WTO mengenai Aspek Hak Harta Intelek Berkaitan Perdagangan (TRIPS). Bersama-sama pertubuhan-pertubuhan ini, CAP telah mengemukakan surat kepada Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, memberi amaran bahawa tuntutan TRIPS-plus oleh EU ini boleh menjejaskan akses kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, melemahkan industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan Malaysia, menyekat hak petani serta mengancam keselamatan makanan. Memandangkan pusingan terkini rundingan Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Malaysia-EU sedang berlangsung dari 21 hingga 25 September 2026, kerajaan mestilah memastikan komitmen perdagangan tidak menyekat keupayaan Malaysia untuk melindungi kesihatan awam serta memelihara kepentingan petani dan pengguna. CAP amat bimbang mengenai cadangan EU berkaitan eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, pelanjutan tempoh paten, rahsia perdagangan, penguatkuasaan hak harta intelek, reka bentuk perindustrian dan perlindungan varieti tumbuhan. Langkah-langkah TRIPS-plus ini boleh melanjutkan perlindungan monopoli, melambatkan persaingan ubat generik serta meningkatkan kos bagi pengguna dan sistem penjagaan kesihatan awam. Harga ubat yang lebih tinggi Cadangan EU bagi melanjutkan tempoh paten sehingga lima tahun akan memanjangkan tempoh monopoli farmaseutikal melebihi tempoh paten 20 tahun yang ditetapkan di bawah TRIPS. Apabila digabungkan dengan peluasan eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, peruntukan sebegini boleh melambatkan kemasukan ubat generik yang mampu milik. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Satu kajian semula pada 2022 terhadap 91 kajian mendapati bahawa monopoli farmaseutikal yang lebih kukuh, yang terhasil daripada peruntukan TRIPS-plus, secara umumnya dikaitkan dengan harga ubat yang lebih tinggi, kelewatan ketersediaan ubat serta peningkatan kos bagi pengguna dan kerajaan. Kajian yang sama menganggarkan bahawa kesan gabungan pelanjutan tempoh paten dan eksklusiviti data di bawah Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Colombia–EU boleh meningkatkan perbelanjaan farmaseutikal Colombia sebanyak $756j pada 2025. Cadangan TRIPS-plus EU juga boleh menjejaskan industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan, yang telah dikenal pasti sebagai sektor penting secara strategik di bawah Pelan Induk Perindustrian Baharu 2030 bagi meningkatkan kemampuan, aksesibiliti dan pengeluaran dalam negara. Malaysia juga merupakan pengimport bersih harta intelek, dengan aliran keluar bersih royalti harta intelek berjumlah kira-kira $2.7bn pada 2024, berbanding penerimaan sebanyak kira-kira $348j. Perlindungan harta intelek yang lebih kukuh dan lebih lama akan meningkatkan aliran keluar royalti serta membebankan pengguna Malaysia, program kesihatan awam dan pengeluar tempatan dengan kos tambahan. “Pada masa belanjawan kesihatan Malaysia telah pun dikurangkan, adalah satu tindakan yang sangat tidak bertanggungjawab bagi kerajaan Malaysia untuk bersetuju dengan cadangan EU yang boleh melonjakkan lagi harga produk perubatan serta menambah beban kewangan kepada rakyat Malaysia dan sistem kesihatan awam yang sedia terbeban,” kata Mohideen Abdul Kader, presiden Persatuan Pengguna-Pengguna Pulau Pinang (CAP). Lindungi hak petani CAP dan 40 pertubuhan masyarakat sivil yang lain turut berasa amat bimbang mengenai cadangan EU yang menuntut Malaysia melindungi varieti tumbuhan selaras dengan Akta 1991 Konvensyen Antarabangsa bagi Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu (Upov). Malaysia sudah pun mempunyai sistem perlindungan varieti tumbuhan sendiri di bawah Akta Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu 2004. Rangka kerja ini melindungi pembiak baka tumbuhan komersial di samping memelihara hak petani untuk menyimpan, menggunakan, menukar dan menjual benih varieti yang dilindungi yang disimpan sendiri. Ia juga mengandungi langkah-langkah perlindungan seperti langkah untuk mencegah biopirasi sumber genetik tumbuhan tempatan, serta memastikan ketersediaan benih pada harga yang berpatutan bagi petani Malaysia. Menyelaraskan sistem Malaysia dengan Upov hanya akan menyumbang kepada penguasaan korporat yang lebih besar dalam sektor benih, dan seterusnya meningkatkan kos benih yang membawa implikasi lebih luas kepada pengguna akibat kenaikan harga makanan, serta menjejaskan keselamatan makanan, kepelbagaian biologi pertanian dan daya tahan sektor pertanian Malaysia. Kepentingan EU adalah untuk meningkatkan akses pasaran bagi syarikat benih Eropah di Malaysia. “Malaysia tidak perlu menerima komitmen TRIPS-plus untuk memuktamadkan perjanjian perdagangan yang bercita-cita tinggi dengan EU,” kata Chee Yoke Ling, pengarah eksekutif Third World Network, salah satu pihak yang turut menandatangani surat kepada perdana menteri itu. “Perjanjian EU dengan India baru-baru ini menunjukkan bahawa adalah mungkin untuk merundingkan perjanjian perdagangan tanpa perlu menyelaraskan dengan Upov 1991 dan bersetuju dengan peruntukan TRIPS-plus seperti pelanjutan tempoh paten, eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, serta kewajipan TRIPS-plus yang lain.” Surat itu menggesa kerajaan untuk: - Menolak semua peruntukan harta intelek (TRIPS-plus yang melangkaui kewajipan WTO Malaysia, termasuk eksklusiviti data dan pemasaran, pelanjutan tempoh paten, perlindungan rahsia perdagangan dan reka bentuk perindustrian yang berlebihan, langkah-langkah sempadan harta intelek yang diperluas serta komitmen Upov - Melindungi ruang dasar Malaysia untuk menggunakan pelesenan wajib, penggunaan oleh kerajaan dan langkah-langkah perlindungan kesihatan awam yang lain - Mengekalkan Akta Perlindungan Varieti Tumbuhan Baharu 2004 dan menolak sebarang komitmen untuk menyelaraskan dengan atau menyertai Upov - Memastikan bahawa perjanjian perdagangan bebas itu tidak menjejaskan akses kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, persaingan ubat generik dan biosimilar, industri farmaseutikal generik tempatan Malaysia, hak petani atau daya tahan sistem pertanian - Memastikan ketelusan serta perundingan yang bermakna dengan masyarakat sivil, pertubuhan pengguna, kumpulan pesakit dan petani pekebun kecil sepanjang proses rundingan berlangsung CAP selanjutnya menyatakan bahawa kebimbangan terperinci telah pun dibangkitkan dengan kementerian berkaitan, termasuk melalui surat yang dihantar oleh Third World Network pada 4 Jun dan oleh Forum Kedaulatan Makanan Malaysia pada 19 Jun. Pertubuhan-pertubuhan masyarakat sivil itu menyatakan bahawa sehingga kini mereka masih belum menerima sebarang maklum balas daripada mana-mana kementerian mengenai status rundingan itu. CAP menggesa kerajaan supaya memastikan Perjanjian Perdagangan Bebas Malaysia-EU tidak mengorbankan akses rakyat Malaysia kepada ubat-ubatan mampu milik, hak petani, keselamatan makanan, mahupun keupayaan Malaysia untuk melaksanakan dasar-dasar demi kepentingan awam. Perjanjian perdagangan mestilah berteraskan kepentingan awam serta memelihara ruang dasar yang diperlukan bagi pembangunan kesihatan, pertanian dan ekonomi Malaysia dalam jangka masa panjang. Antara pihak yang menandatangani surat itu ialah Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Majlis Aids Malaysia (MAC), Yayasan Aids Malaysia (MAF), Forum Kedaulatan Makanan Malaysia (FKMM) dan Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) – cawangan Malaysia; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia (PPIM); Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM); serta Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September English version EU-Malaysia trade deal must not put affordable medical products, farmers’ rights and food security at risk The Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP) and 40 other Malaysian civil society organisations call on the Malaysian government to reject intellectual property demands by the EU that go beyond Malaysia’s obligations under the World Trade Organization’s on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS). Together with these organizations, CAP has sent a letter to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, warning that these TRIPS-plus demands of the EU could undermine access to affordable medicines, weaken Malaysia’s domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, restrict farmers’ rights and threaten food security. With the latest round of the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement negotiations taking place from 21 to 25 September, the government must ensure that trade commitments do not restrict Malaysia’s ability to protect public health, and safeguard the interests of farmers and consumers. CAP is particularly concerned about the EU’s proposals on data and marketing exclusivity, patent-term extension, trade secrets, intellectual property enforcement, industrial designs and plant variety protection. These TRIPS-plus measures could extend monopoly protection, delay generic competition and increase costs for consumers and the public healthcare system. Higher medicine prices competition The EU’s proposals for patent-term extensions of up to five years would extend pharmaceutical monopolies beyond the 20-year patent term required under TRIPS. Combined with expanded data and marketing exclusivity, such provisions could delay the entry of affordable generic medicines. A 2022 review of 91 studies found that stronger pharmaceutical monopolies created through TRIPS-plus provisions are generally associated with higher drug prices, delayed availability and increased costs for consumers and governments. The same review estimated that the combined impact of patent-term extensions and data exclusivity under the Colombia–EU Free Trade Agreement could increase Colombia’s pharmaceutical spending by $756m in 2025. The EU’s TRIPS-plus proposals can also undermine the domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, which has been identified as strategically important under the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 for improving affordability, accessibility and domestic production. Malaysia is also a net importer of intellectual property, with about $2.7bn in net intellectual property royalty outflows in 2024, compared with around $348m in receipts. Stronger and longer intellectual property protection would increase royalty outflows and impose additional costs on local consumers, public health programmes and domestic manufacturers. “At a time when Malaysia’s health budget has already been cut, it would be deeply irresponsible for the Malaysian government to agree to EU proposals that could further drive up the prices of medical products and place additional financial burdens on the Malaysian people and on an already stretched public health system,” said Mohideen Abdul Kader, president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang. Protect farmers’ rights CAP and the other 40 civil society organisations are also deeply concerned about the EU’s proposal requiring Malaysia to protect plant varieties in accordance with the 1991 Act of the International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (Upov). Malaysia already has its own plant variety protection system under the Protection of New Plant Varieties Act 2004. This framework protects commercial plant breeders while preserving farmers’ rights to save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seeds of protected varieties. It also contains safeguards such as measures to prevent biopiracy of local plant genetic resources, and ensure the availability of seeds at reasonable prices for Malaysian farmers. Aligning Malaysia’s system with Upov will only contribute to greater corporate concentration in the seed sector, and consequently increase the costs of seeds with wider implications for consumers as food prices increase, food security, agrobiodiversity and the resilience of Malaysian agriculture. The EU’s interest is to increase market access for European seed companies in Malaysia. “Malaysia does not need to accept TRIPS-plus commitments to conclude an ambitious EU trade agreement,” said Chee Yoke Ling, the executive director of Third World Network, another signatory to the letter to the prime minister. “Recent EU agreement with India demonstrates that it is possible to negotiate a trade agreement without having to align with Upov 1991 and agree to TRIPS-plus provisions such as patent-term extension, data and marketing exclusivity, and other TRIPS-plus obligations.” The letter calls on the government to: - Reject all TRIPS-plus intellectual property provisions that go beyond Malaysia’s WTO obligations, including data and marketing exclusivity, patent-term extensions, excessive trade-secret and industrial-design protection, expanded intellectual property border measures and Upov commitments - Protect Malaysia’s policy space to use compulsory licensing, government use and other public health safeguards - Maintain the Protection of New Plant Varieties Act 2004 and reject any commitment to align with or accede to Upov - Ensure that the free trade agreement does not undermine access to affordable medicines, generic and biosimilar competition, Malaysia’s domestic generic pharmaceutical industry, farmers’ rights or the resilience of the agricultural system - Ensure transparency and meaningful consultation with civil society, consumer organisations, patient groups and smallholder farmers throughout the negotiations CAP further notes that detailed concerns have already been raised with the relevant ministries, including through letters sent by Third World Network on 4 June and by the Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum on 19 June. The civil society organisations state that, to date, they have not received a response from any ministry concerning the status of the negotiations. CAP urges the government to ensure that the Malaysia–EU free trade agreement does not trade away Malaysians’ access to affordable medicines, farmers’ rights, food security or Malaysia’s ability to pursue public interest policies. Trade agreements must serve the public interest and preserve the policy space needed for Malaysia’s long-term health, agricultural and economic development. Signatories to the letter include the Malaysian Agroecology Society – SRI-Mas, Malaysian Aids Council, Malaysian Aids Foundation, Malaysian Food Sovereignty Forum, Malaysian Rare Disorders Society; Médecins Sans Frontières Malaysian chapter; Persatuan Pengguna Islam Malaysia; Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth) – SAM; and Together Against Cancer Association. – CAP, 25 September Mohideen Abdul Kader is the president of the Consumers’ Association of Penang (CAP). title: Assault on constitutional sovereignty of Negeri Sembilan monarchy and rule of law – 10 former bar presidents
body: We are a country of laws. Yet several events of the past few days have wrought chaos upon the sanctity of the rule of law and the institutions established under the Federal Constitution. On 16 September Malaysians were shocked by the news that the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had purportedly been deposed unilaterally and unceremoniously by the Negeri Sembilan state executive council, without any stated grounds, due process or enquiry. The reported conduct of the executive council is an egregious violation of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and a direct and unlawful assault on the institution of the constitutional monarchy. The removal of a reigning constitutional sovereign is an extraordinary measure of the gravest constitutional consequence. Political expediency, backroom manoeuvres and unilateral executive decrees can never be a substitute for due process. In Negeri Sembilan, that removal process is strictly governed by Article 10 of the state constitution, which stipulates three conditions. The first condition for initiating the removal of the ruler is the holding of a “full and complete enquiry by the Undangs” to establish whether valid and sufficient grounds exist for such an extraordinary course of action. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Based on media reports, there has been no evidence that any enquiry was ever conducted. No charges or grounds of misconduct have ever been made known to the public. Most crucially, it appears that His Royal Highness was never notified of any allegations, let alone afforded the elementary right to be heard. Attempts by the executive council to assert that an enquiry was held do not stand up to scrutiny, having been advanced only belatedly and without any explanation as to whether His Royal Highness was notified or given any opportunity to be heard. In any event, such an alleged enquiry cannot constitute the “full and complete enquiry by the Undangs” required under Article 10(1) of the state constitution. The second and third conditions stipulate that a proclamation must be executed “under the hands of the Undangs and the Menteri Besar”. Serious questions arise as to the validity, propriety and legality of the purported proclamation dated 19 April, which has been denounced by the former menteri besar, Aminuddin Harun; and disavowed by the current menteri besar, Ismail Lasim, who has stated that he signed it under duress, and in respect of which he has lodged a police report. Further, if the purported proclamation is dated 19 April but was signed by this menteri besar only on 3 August, this raises a fundamental question as to its validity, given that he was not the menteri besar on 19 April. The executive council’s announcement on 16 September smacks of blatant executive overreach. The executive council possesses no constitutional mandate, jurisdiction or power to unseat a ruler. Any such unilateral pronouncement is an ultra vires act that strikes at the very foundation of the constitutional order. It is noteworthy that the invalidity of the proclamation has been affirmed by the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang and, separately, by the Attorney General’s Chambers. The state secretary’s office has likewise concurred with the latter’s position and declined to proceed with the gazetting of the purported proclamation. We, the undersigned, call for an immediate and complete halt to this assault on the constitutional sovereignty of the Negeri Sembilan monarchy and the rule of law. We strongly urge the state government of Negeri Sembilan, all public officials, and all citizens of Malaysia to faithfully uphold the Federal Constitution and the state constitution, preserve the rule of law, and fully respect the sovereignty and constitutional standing of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the sole, lawful, and reigning Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan. The state executive council is not above the law, and its unlawful conduct in this matter must be curbed. We call on the federal government to step in and finally resolve these troubling issues. This state of affairs sets a dangerous precedent for the constitutional monarchy and the future of this country – a country that must, at all times, chart its course strictly in accordance with the law. Such unbecoming and undignified conduct, as well as such utter disrespect for the law, must stop. Issued by the following former presidents of the Malaysian Bar on 21 September: Mah Weng Kwai, Kuthubul Zaman Bukhari, Yeo Yang Poh, Ambiga Sreenevasan, Ragunath Kesavan, Lim Chee Wee, Christopher Leong, George Varughese, Salim Bashir, and Karen Cheah Yee Lynn The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: MACC Remands Corporate Brothers in RM10m Investment Probe, Seizes 15 Luxury Cars Among Others
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Two corporate figures, who are brothers, are being remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective from Thursday until next Monday (Oct 5), from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court on Thursday morning. According to a source, the two men, in their 40s and 50s and carrying the titles of Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira respectively, were detained at about 9pm on Wednesday after giving their statements at the MACC headquarters here. Initial investigations found that the duo were suspected of acting in collusion in the alleged offence in late 2020. “They are also believed to have colluded with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve an investment of about RM10 million in an investment company owned by the elder brother,” the source told Bernama. The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter when contacted and said the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. title: Maybank Foundation marks a decade of empowering weavers with third regional natural dye workshop and gallery launch in Cambodia | Maybank
body: Workshop and gallery launch strengthens natural dyeing knowledge and Cambodia's silk weaving heritage, building on a decade of empowering 2,617 women weavers and supporting 3,024 farmers across ASEAN Maybank Foundation, the social impact arm of Maybank Group, together with Maybank Cambodia and local programme implementation partner, Color Silk, recently marked the conclusion of the third Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) Regional Natural Dye Workshop and officially launched the MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery at the Maybank Silk Weaving Training Centre in Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. Held from 25 to 28 September 2026, the four-day workshop brought together women weavers and MWEW programme partners from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines to exchange traditional natural dyeing knowledge, strengthen technical skills and advance sustainable textile practices across ASEAN. The workshop and gallery launch form part of MWEW’s tenth anniversary milestones, celebrating a decade of preserving traditional woven textile heritage, strengthening women’s economic independence and supporting sustainable livelihoods across the region. The closing ceremony and gallery launch brought together 80 guests, including Her Excellency Srey Siyut, Advisor to the Governor, National Bank of Cambodia; Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women's Affairs Cambodia; His Excellency Prem Rotha, Deputy Governor of Siem Reap Province; Mr Me Sambo, Deputy Director of Department of Culture and Fine Arts in Siem Reap, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts; Mr Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia; Ms Qazreen Chan, Chief Operating Officer of Maybank Cambodia; Ms Noor Fadzlin Ariffin, Head, Community Empowerment of Maybank Foundation; Ms Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk, representatives from Maybank Cambodia, Maybank Foundation, regional MWEW programme partners and weavers, and Color Silk weavers. The ceremony also featured the presentation of certificates to workshop participants, a sharing session with three Cambodian graduate weavers and a gathering of representatives from all 10 MWEW programme batches in Cambodia. Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women’s Affairs, Cambodia, tries her hand at the traditional loom, as other attendees look on. As part of the MWEW programme, looms are provided by Color Silk to weavers upon completion of their training, enabling them to continue weaving from home and generate income towards greater financial independence. Ten years of strengthening women’s livelihoods and Cambodia’s weaving heritage Cambodia has been an integral part of MWEW since its introduction in 2016. Through its longstanding partnership with Color Silk, Maybank Foundation has supported the preservation of traditional Cambodian silk weaving while equipping women from underserved communities with skills and opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods and greater economic independence. As of 30 June 2026, MWEW in Cambodia has trained 852 women weavers, supported 1,584 farmers and facilitated the planting of approximately 220,700 mulberry trees to sustain local sericulture and silk production. Beneficiaries have also recorded monthly income increases of up to USD350, demonstrating how traditional craftsmanship can create tangible economic opportunities for women and their communities. Izlyn Ramli, CEO of Maybank Foundation and Head of Group Corporate Affairs, Maybank said, “Over the past decade, Maybank Women Eco-Weavers has shown that preserving traditional weaving heritage can go hand in hand with strengthening women’s economic independence and creating sustainable livelihoods. What began as an initiative for women weavers has grown into a livelihood and value-chain ecosystem connecting women, farmers and communities across five ASEAN countries through shared knowledge, skills and opportunities. “The third Regional Natural Dye Workshop and launch of the Natural Dye Gallery in Cambodia build on this journey. It is especially meaningful that the gallery was funded and developed through the eMpowering Youths Across ASEAN (eYAA) Cohort 4 programme with Color Silk, bringing together youth volunteers and communities to create a lasting resource for women weavers and farmers. This reflects the kind of lasting impact we seek to create through Maybank Foundation, where collaboration creates opportunities for communities to thrive while preserving ASEAN’s cultural and environmental heritage for generations to come,” she added. Advancing regional collaboration through natural dyeing The third MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop builds on a regional knowledge-sharing platform established in 2024 to strengthen traditional natural dyeing expertise and promote more sustainable textile production across MWEW communities. The first workshop in Sarawak, Malaysia in 2024 brought together 47 programme partners and weavers from four countries, resulting in 69 natural hues. In 2025, the second edition expanded participation to all five MWEW countries, with 77 women weavers developing 158 natural hues through exchanges on natural dyeing, local biodiversity and sustainable community practices. Hosted by Color Silk, the 2026 workshop brought together 50 participants to explore locally sourced botanical materials and traditional techniques for working with silk and cotton. The workshop culminated in more than 18 natural hues, while strengthening connections between women artisans, farmers and communities involved in the cultivation and supply of natural dye materials. From ASEAN youth initiative to a lasting resource for Cambodian communities The MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery builds on the Natural Dye Laboratory and Planting (NDLP) project launched in 2024 under Cohort 4 of eMpowering Youths Across ASEAN (eYAA), jointly implemented by Maybank Foundation and ASEAN Foundation. Through the project, Color Silk worked with 10 ASEAN youth volunteers and the local community in Siem Reap to promote sustainable dyeing practices and create economic opportunities for women weavers and farmers. The initiative benefited 215 community members, engaged 38 students in tree planting, provided 40 households with dye trees, supported the planting of 420 dye trees and engaged 17 local community members in constructing the gallery. Sixteen women weavers from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines completed the 3rd MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop, unlocking 18 colours through natural dyeing techniques. The hands-on exchange strengthens practical knowledge and sustainable weaving practices across MWEW’s ASEAN community. Officially launched two years after its establishment, the gallery is equipped with natural dye processing facilities and will serve as a hub for Color Silk’s weavers and wider community, supporting hands-on learning, experimentation, knowledge-sharing and the showcasing of locally developed natural dye products. The facility connects the outcomes of an ASEAN youth-led initiative with MWEW’s longer-term commitment to strengthening women’s livelihoods and sustainable weaving practices in Cambodia. Ms Vanntha Ngorn, Founder of Color Silk, said, “For our women weavers, traditional silk weaving is more than a craft. It is a source of livelihood, cultural identity and knowledge passed down through generations. Natural dyeing is an important part of this heritage, and the gallery provides a space for our community to continue learning, experimenting and strengthening these traditional skills. “What makes this facility particularly meaningful is how it was developed through the collective efforts of ASEAN youth volunteers and our local community. Their contributions have helped establish a resource that can continue supporting our women weavers and farmers, while encouraging younger generations to appreciate and preserve Cambodia’s traditional textile heritage,” she added. Ms Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk (with microphone), explains to distinguished guests on the natural dyeing process which uses locally sourced materials such as coconut husks, seeds and neem leaves to extract natural colours at the newly launched gallery. The space of the MWEW Color Silk Natural Dye Gallery is designed to facilitate hands-on learning and the continued sharing of traditional dyeing knowledge. Mr Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia, “Cambodia’s silk weaving heritage is an important part of our cultural identity, and preserving this tradition means continuing to invest in the women, farmers and communities who sustain it. Through our longstanding collaboration with Maybank Foundation and Color Silk, we have seen how traditional skills can create meaningful economic opportunities while keeping an important part of Cambodia’s heritage alive. “The Natural Dye Gallery represents another step forward in this journey. By bringing together traditional craftsmanship, sustainable practices and the contributions of ASEAN youth, we are creating opportunities for our weaving communities to continue developing their skills while preserving this valuable knowledge for future generations.” Celebrating a decade of growing together across ASEAN Since its launch in 2016, MWEW has grown into a regional economic ecosystem spanning Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia and the Philippines. As of 30 June 2026, it has trained 2,617 women weavers and supported 3,024 farmers, with USD5.6 million (RM22.9 million) invested across traditional weaving, natural fibre cultivation, natural dyeing, skills development, sustainable production and market access. Participants received their certificates at the completion ceremony of the 3rd MWEW Regional Natural Dye Workshop, joined by representatives from the Cambodian government, Maybank Cambodia, Maybank Foundation and Color Silk. The workshop reflects MWEW’s continued commitment to connecting communities through shared knowledge and sustainable craft practices. Witnessing the certificate presentation ceremony are (Back row); His Excellency Prem Rotha, Deputy Governor of Siem Reap Province (in dark blue suit with glasses); Her Excellency Sovuth Sopahnarath, Undersecretary of State, Ministry of Women's Affairs Cambodia (in teal blue dress); Her Excellency Srey Siyut, Advisor to the Governor, National Bank of Cambodia (in dark brown dress); Mr. Rath Sophoan, Chief Executive Officer and Country Head of Maybank Cambodia (in yellow and black shirt); Mr. Me Sambo, Deputy Director of Department of Culture and Fine Arts in Siem Reap, Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts (in black suit with white shirt and light blue neck tie); Ms. Ngorn Vanntha, Founder of Color Silk (in light brown dress); Ms. Qazreen Chan, Chief Operating Officer of Maybank Cambodia (in black and white blazer jacket); Ms. Noor Fadzlin Ariffin, Head, Community Empowerment of Maybank Foundation (in black cardigan) and Mr. Johann Nawawi, MWEW Architect Benefactor (in light brown batik shirt). Following its tenth anniversary celebration in Bali in August 2026, the third Regional Natural Dye Workshop carries this milestone into Cambodia, bringing regional knowledge and collaboration directly to its weaving communities. MWEW also advances Maybank Group’s ROAR30 sustainability ambitions by supporting inclusive economic participation, sustainable livelihoods and resilient communities while preserving ASEAN’s cultural heritage.

title: Expedite political will to guarantee people’s right to know
body: On the International Day for Universal Access to Information on 28 September, the Centre for Independent Journalism (CIJ), Article 19 and the Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center) call on the Malaysian government and Parliament to make the right to access information a meaningful and accessible right, and not merely a promise of reform. The UN has designated this year’s theme as ‘Upholding information integrity in the digital age: the role of access to information in addressing information disorder’. Reliable, timely and credible public information is essential to informed participation, accountability and trust in public institutions. Malaysia stands at a critical juncture. Parliament is considering the nation’s first federal freedom of information law, while serious questions remain about the transparency, legal basis, and implementation of Najib Razak’s conditional pardon and house arrest. These are not separate transparency failures. They expose the same problem: Malaysians cannot hold institutions accountable when the government makes decisions behind a wall of secrecy. We acknowledge the government’s decision to introduce a federal Freedom of Information Bill and welcome its referral to a parliamentary special select committee following its first reading in July 2026. However, as our organisations have stated, the bill, as tabled, falls far short of what ordinary people should expect from landmark transparency legislation. The Centre for Law and Democracy’s assessment subsequently gave the bill 47 out of 150 points under its right to information rating methodology, highlighting the extent to which the proposed framework needs improvement. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member The bill must be strengthened into an enforceable right to know act, consistent with Article 10(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution, international law and standards and the recommendations of Malaysian and international civil society. Malaysia must end the culture of secrecy that continues to shield the exercise of power from public scrutiny. The government cannot credibly champion transparency while limiting the public’s access to information about decisions of profound public interest, including from the laws governing access to information itself. The government must demonstrate its political will and commitment to transparency by applying these principles across the board and not letting them remain mere lip service to garner votes. On this International Day for Universal Access to Information, we call on the government and Parliament to act. The government and Parliament must: Strengthen the bill, currently under the purview of the special select committee, into an enforceable right to know act, consistent with international laws and standards and the recommendations from civil society groups. It must: - Uphold the constitutional guarantee under Article 10(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution and guarantee freedom of information as a pre-condition to the realisation of the freedom of expression and speech - Make disclosure the rule and secrecy the exception, with narrowly defined exemptions based on demonstrable harm and subject to a strong public-interest override - Ensure the freedom of information law cannot be undermined by existing secrecy provisions, including the Official Secrets Act - Remove unnecessary restrictions on who can request information and ensure everyone can exercise the right without having to demonstrate a particular interest or purpose - Establish a freedom of information commission as an independent oversight body, with the power to review refusals, order disclosure and monitor the implementation of the freedom of information law - Require proactive disclosure of information and documents of significant public interest - Make the parliamentary freedom of information process transparent and participatory, including publication of submissions, recommendations and the revised bill Guarantee prompt disclosure and publication of the documents necessary for the public to understand the decision regarding the conditional pardon of Najib Razak, as demanded by CIJ and other civil society organisations, including: - The relevant pardons board minutes - The Attorney General’s written submission, subject only to narrowly justified redactions - The full conditions governing the house arrest arrangement - The legal basis for implementing house arrest and its relationship with existing laws - The mechanisms for monitoring and enforcing compliance - Significant public expenditure associated with the arrangement. These demands do not challenge the constitutional existence of the power of pardon. They demand transparency about the exercise and implementation of authority’s power. Constitutional powers are not a licence for institutional secrecy. The Government has repeatedly committed itself to institutional reform, good governance and restoring public confidence. The test of those commitments is whether transparency is upheld when disclosure is difficult, politically sensitive or institutionally consequential. We believe that a freedom of information law that leaves the underlying culture of secrecy intact will not deliver meaningful reform. In the spirit of this international day, we call on Malaysia to move from promises of transparency to a legally enforceable culture of openness. Ordinary people have the right to know. Disclosure of information held by government and public authorities is necessary to scrutinise the exercise of public power. This ensures that no institution is beyond legitimate public accountability. The right to information is not a concession from government. It is a foundation of accountable government. This legislation is essential to guarantee the public’s collective right to be informed by public authorities about important aspects of their functioning; the right to seek or request information; and the right to be informed and to receive information about various aspects of the public sphere. We are also pleased to launch our campaign demonstrating the level of support from our MPs for the guarantee of a robust bill. Look out for more information on our social media in the coming days. Issued by: - Wathshlah Naidu, Centre for Independent Journalism - Nalini Elumalai, Article 19 - Prishanth Linggaraj, C4 Center The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: High Court Dissolves Genneva, Paving Way for Victims to Settle Claims
body: SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses. In her brief judgment on Wednesday, judge Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business. The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors. The court granted the winding-up order and confirmed interim liquidator Wong Weng Foo to his role in dissolving the firm. Ng Wan Yee, who holds a major stake of 750,000 shares in the company, had moved to wind up the company in August 2024, to prevent other company directors from removing more than RM21 million in released company assets. The move follows a Sessions Court order on June 28, 2024, that revoked seizure orders under anti-money laundering laws on millions of ringgit and approximately 28.3kg of gold bars. In her petition, Wan Yee said there was a "high likelihood" that functional directors or other relevant parties might dissipate these assets for personal benefit rather than settling claims of thousands of investors. She claimed that some directors had already attempted to "siphon monies" under the guise of paying professional fees. An opposing creditor, Liew Chio Chuan, a 25% shareholder of Genneva, had challenged the appointment of Wong, arguing there was "material non-disclosure" by Wan Yee and that there was "no real danger" of assets being lost before a formal hearing before the court. Central to the dispute was the movement of funds just days before the petition was filed. Records show that following the release of the seizure orders, Genneva's directors had authorised the transfer of RM11,659,661.20 from accounts at Maybank and Public Bank to a stakeholder account held by the company’s long-time solicitors, Messrs Gooi & Azura. The solicitors and Maybank have justified the transfers, citing a board resolution dated June 26, 2024, and "letters of authorisation" dating back to 2016. They maintain the bank was unaware of the pending winding-up petition at the time. Genneva and its top executives were found guilty in August 2020 of illegally taking tens of million in deposits. The company was fined RM450 million and various executives were also jailed and slapped with fines amounting to hundreds of millions of ringgit. Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad launched Genneva's "syariah-compliant" gold trading scheme on Dec 15, 2010. title: DNB secures RM5.2 bil for next phase of 5G growth, MOF retains special share
body: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion financing exercise as it moves into the next phase of Malaysia’s 5G development. The financing comes as the nation’s first 5G network has secured a new long-term spectrum assignment, while the government (via MOF Inc) will exit as an ordinary shareholder. CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal ownership in DNB. Transition is expected to be completed in early Q4 2026, however, MOF Inc. will retain a special share. DNB completes RM5.2 billion financing DNB said it has completed a RM5.2 billion Syndicated Islamic Term Financing exercise, which it described as among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank acted as Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner and Coordinating Arranger, while AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank and United Overseas Bank Malaysia were Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing will also be used to refinance DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on 29 September 2026. According to DNB, the new financing provides a sustainable long-term funding structure to support its future growth. The financing is also expected to reduce the need for additional equity funding from DNB’s mobile network operator shareholders, based on DNB’s current regulatory commitments and funding requirements. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets.” He added, “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the Government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” DNB gets 15-year 5G spectrum certainty DNB has also received the full 100MHz block in the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz band, known as F0, while its entire 240MHz spectrum holding has been converted from Apparatus Assignment (AA) into Spectrum Assignment (SA). The Spectrum Assignment for a 15-year period awarded by the MCMC provides greater long-term certainty over spectrum availability and it takes effect from 1 October 2026. By securing 200MHz of the contiguous mid-band spectrum (3.3 to 3.5GHz), DNB has a stronger foundation to modernise the network, expand indoor building solutions, enhance coverage and maximise spectrum utilisation. In addition, DNB also has 2x 20Hz blocks of the low band spectrum with 703MHz to 723MHz and 758Hz to 778MHz. DNB said its spectrum holdings will also support higher network capacity and efficiency, as well as technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. MOF to retain special share in DNB While the recent financing facilitates MOF Inc.’s planned exit as an ordinary shareholder of DNB, the government via MOF Inc will continue to retain a special share in the company. According to DNB, the special share will safeguard national interests and ensure continued stewardship over key strategic matters. Following the share transfer, the mobile network operator shareholders would assume a greater role in jointly steering DNB’s strategic and operational priorities. In a separate statement issued by CelcomDigi, the telco says it will bring its scale, nationwide network assets and more than 30 years of telecommunications experience to support DNB. This includes leveraging on existing infrastructure, sites and capabilities to drive cost efficiencies, support coverage expansion and accelerate indoor 5G deployment.

MOF to retain special share in DNB While the recent financing facilitates MOF Inc.’s planned exit as an ordinary shareholder of DNB, the government via MOF Inc will continue to retain a special share in the company. According to DNB, the special share will safeguard national interests and ensure continued stewardship over key strategic matters. Following the share transfer, the mobile network operator shareholders would assume a greater role in jointly steering DNB’s strategic and operational priorities. In a separate statement issued by CelcomDigi, the telco says it will bring its scale, nationwide network assets and more than 30 years of telecommunications experience to support DNB. This includes leveraging on existing infrastructure, sites and capabilities to drive cost efficiencies, support coverage expansion and accelerate indoor 5G deployment.

body: SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Gold Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses.  In her brief judgment on Wednesday, Justice Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business.  The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors.  The court granted the winding-up order and confirmed interim liquidator Wong Weng Foo to his role in dissolving the firm.  Ng Wan Yee, who holds a major stake of 750,000 shares in the company, had moved to wind up the company in August 2024, to prevent other company directors from removing more than RM21 million in released company assets.  The move follows a Sessions Court order on June 28, 2024, that revoked seizure orders under anti-money laundering laws on millions of ringgit and approximately 28.3kg of gold bars.  In her petition, Wan Yee said there was a "high likelihood" that functional directors or other relevant parties might dissipate these assets for personal benefit rather than settling claims of thousands of investors.  She claimed that some directors had already attempted to "siphon monies" under the guise of paying professional fees.  An opposing creditor, Liew Chio Chuan, a 25% shareholder of Genneva, had challenged the appointment of Wong, arguing there was "material non-disclosure" by Wan Yee and that there was "no real danger" of assets being lost before a formal hearing before the court.  Central to the dispute was the movement of funds just days before the petition was filed.  Records show that following the release of the seizure orders, Genneva's directors had authorised the transfer of RM11,659,661.20 from accounts at Maybank and Public Bank to a stakeholder account held by the company’s long-time solicitors, Messrs Gooi & Azura.  The solicitors and Maybank have justified the transfers, citing a board resolution dated June 26, 2024, and "letters of authorisation" dating back to 2016. They maintain the bank was unaware of the pending winding-up petition at the time.  Genneva Gold and its top executives were found guilty in August 2020 of illegally taking tens of million in deposits. The company was fined RM450 million and various executives were also jailed and slapped with fines amounting to hundreds of millions of ringgit.  Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad launched Genneva Malaysia Sdn Bhd’s "syariah-compliant" gold trading scheme on Dec 15, 2010.

title: Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Oil and gas, Sorento Capital Bhd, Bermaz Auto Bhd, UMedic Group Bhd
body:
This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026

Oil and gas

OVERWEIGHT

HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Brent has returned above US$100 per barrel as risks rise across Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi’s East-West Pipeline, while Middle East supply disruptions have widened the global oil deficit. China crude imports are also recovering, adding further upside risk to prices. We now expect Brent at US$95-US$100 per barrel towards end-2026 and raise our 2026 assumption to US$90 per barrel from US$80 per barrel.

While we retain “buy” calls on most names, we remain selective and favour companies with earnings drivers that can sustain beyond near-term Brent volatility.

We advocate positioning for our 2027 thesis of a recovery in Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s (PETRONAS) upstream capital expenditure (capex) alongside rising regional energy-security investments. We believe the sector remains supported by a recovery in offshore support vessel-related names such as Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd (KL:DAYANG), Keyfield International Bhd (KL:KEYFIELD) and Perdana Petroleum Bhd (KL:PERDANA), while improving oil and gas services and equipment order flows and longer-term demand for storage, pipelines and broader energy infrastructure should continue to support Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) and Wasco Bhd (KL:WASCO).

Dialog remains our top pick. We expect Dialog’s earnings to remain well supported in FY27-FY28 by growth across its three key segments. Upstream will be supported by the new Cendramas production sharing contract and Baram Junior Cluster (both commencing from 2QFY27), which are expected to shift the upstream earnings mix higher to 30% to 40%. Meanwhile, Dialog’s downstream earnings visibility remains well supported by several ongoing engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning projects.

PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd’s (KL:PCHEM) (PetChem) share price has risen around 25% after we upgraded it to “buy” in our end-June report. We are seeing early signs of stabilisation in key product prices, while elevated Brent prices could support further improvement in overall average selling prices in 4QFY26. We expect utilisation rates to improve with minimal turnaround activities at Methanol 2 for 60 days and Fertiliser Sabah for 10 days in 3QFY26, while no scheduled plant turnaround is expected in 4QFY26. PetChem remains attractive, with recovery of urea prices in 2HFY27 as seasonal planting demand returns, and potential divestment of its Pengerang Petrochemical Co Sdn Bhd stake, which could remove significant earnings drag and reduce the group’s foreign exchange (forex) exposure.

We view Dayang as a key beneficiary of a potential PETRONAS upstream capex recovery in 2027. Dayang delivered a stronger performance in 2024, when PETRONAS’ upstream spending was relatively elevated at around RM21.5 billion across 2023-2024, while upstream capex remained subdued at only RM9 billion in 1HFY26.

Sorento Capital Bhd

Target price: 77 sen BUY

TA SECURITIES (SEPT 14): Sorento Capital Bhd’s (KL:SORENTO) FY26 gross profit margin reached 45.2%, the highest in the company’s history, despite challenging market conditions arising from the US-Iran war. Management attributes the margin expansion to a reduction in original equipment manufacturing cost in China late last year, which contributed to a stronger 47% gross profit margin in 4QFY26.

According to management, global brass prices rose by 50% following the onset of the US-Iran war, leading to higher production cost for bathroom and kitchen taps. However, prices of ceramic bathroom products have been undergoing price cutting. As China’s exports of ceramic products to the Middle East has been disrupted by the war, these products have been redirected to Asian markets, creating downward price pressure. As such, management is confident of sustaining its gross profit margin above 40% for FY27.

As far as project sales are concerned, the group has seen an uptick in orders for its Sorento-series sanitary ware. It order book has increased to RM150 million from RM120 million, and we expect the company to secure new orders of RM80 million each in FY27 and FY28.

Bermaz Auto Bhd

Target price: RM1.35 BUY

MAYBANK INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Bermaz Auto Bhd’s (KL:BAUTO) recovery trajectory continues to outperform market expectations, and we see further upside should the momentum sustain.

Near-term margins should improve with stronger support from XPeng China, while Mazda volumes remain resilient. Key considerations include completely built-up (CBU) supply and evolving earnings mix as completely knocked-down (CKD) ramps up.

Mazda CBU volume now contributes about two-thirds of sales, which we expect to sustain over the next few quarters until the all-new CX-5 CKD is launched in mid-2027. We expect 5,000 CBU units by year-end, while forex hedging should support CBU margins in FY27.

Overall, BAuto’s outlook is underpinned by new Mazda and XPeng model launches, supporting its FY27 sales target of 16,000 units (+23% y-o-y, ex-Kia sales in FY26). Associate earnings are also improving, with Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd returning to profitability and further supported by potential additional assembly contracts. Mazda Malaysia should benefit from CKD expansion, with export volume for the new CX-5 from 2027 (targeting 7,000 units per annum) providing an additional volume boost, while Kia exposure is now minimal. Near-term earnings visibility remains solid, combined with an attractive dividend yield of more than 9%.

UMedic Group Bhd

Target price: 43 sen BUY

MBSB RESEARCH (SEPT 15): The RM47 billion allocated under Budget 2026 and the 13th Malaysia Plan promise of RM40 billion until 2030 continue to support UMedic Group Bhd (KL:UMC).

We believe with the upcoming Budget 2027 — which is expected to continue prioritising citizens’ welfare — UMC is positioned for sustained long-term growth by leveraging key industry tailwinds, including hospital overcrowding, medical tourism and an ageing population projected to reach 21% by 2044.

To capitalise on these trends, UMC is expected to further expand into ambulatory care by growing its ambulance fleet, scaling its integrated learning and community health centres, and diversifying into the laboratory market and specialised verticals via its Akiteck and Ateria subsidiaries.

Additionally, UMC is reinforcing its manufacturing foundation by acquiring three acres of industrial land, expanding clean room capacity and adopting advanced automation to meet rising domestic and global demand across its product portfolio.

By incorporating UMC’s FY26 results into our valuation, we revised FY27-FY28 earnings forecasts upwards by 2%. We like UMC for its stable distribution business, paired with its high-margin proprietary manufacturing operations. UMC’s key drivers remain the government’s fiscal support and long-term demographic tailwinds in terms of care demand and medical tourism.

title: Kuala Lumpur News
body:
JETOUR Launches T2 i-DM Hybrid

JETOUR Malaysia has launched the T2 i-DM, a plug-in hybrid SUV priced at RM162,800.
It pairs a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine with a dual-motor electric system for a combined output of up to 265kW and 610Nm. JETOUR claims up to 1,200km of combined driving range and more than 100km on electric power alone. The battery is an 18.4kWh lithium iron phosphate unit, and DC fast charging takes it from 30% to 80% in 27 minutes or less, according to the company.
The first 2,000 customers get an Early Bird Package worth up to RM3,000, with a choice of a free 7kW wallbox charger with installation or RM2,000 in ChargeSini charging credit, plus a free V2L adapter cable. Financing rates start at 1.68%, subject to terms and conditions.
The car comes with a seven-year or 150,000km vehicle warranty, an eight-year or 160,000km battery warranty and five free services.

New Jalan Alor Seafood Restaurant

Canteen Malaya has opened on Jalan Alor in Kuala Lumpur, offering live seafood and an open kitchen in an air-conditioned, four-level restaurant.
Diners choose their own crab, tiger prawns or fish, which is then cooked to order in view of the dining floor. Crab is the focus of the menu, with more than 30 flavours and preparations, including 12 signature dishes such as Salted Egg Crab, Kam Heong Crab and White Pepper Crab.
The restaurant seats up to 700 guests. The ground and first floors hold the dining areas and private rooms, and the second floor has an event hall for up to 250.
“Our focus is simple: to serve fresh, honest seafood to everyday diners,” said Ms Patricia Wong, Management Representative of Canteen Malaya. “We wanted an open kitchen where guests can watch their seafood being prepared, in a space where they can take their time over a meal.”
Canteen Malaya is at 28, 28A-C, 30 and 30A-C Jalan Alor and is open daily from 11am to 2am.

L&G AGM Backs Growth Push

Land & General Berhad (L&G) secured shareholder approval for all nine resolutions at its 63rd AGM today, including a final dividend of 0.8 sen per share for FY2026. Combined with the 0.2 sen interim dividend paid in May, total FY2026 dividends reached 1.0 sen — up 25% from FY2025. The final dividend is payable 16 October to shareholders on record as at 2 October.
Shareholders also approved the re-election of three directors, the reappointment of KPMG PLT as auditors, a general share issuance mandate, and a proposed share buy-back.
The vote follows a record FY2026: Group revenue rose 70.6% to RM490.5 million, pre-tax profit climbed 25.6% to RM74.2 million, and net profit attributable to owners grew 38.7% to RM50.5 million. The momentum carried into 1QFY2027, with revenue up 61.5% year-on-year to RM159.0 million and net profit up 88.7% to RM21.5 million. Unbilled sales stood at RM513 million as at 30 June, backed by RM1.5 billion in planned FY2027 launches.
L&G is also broadening beyond its traditional property development base into a three-pillar structure spanning property, education (via its Sri Bestari schools) and industrial development. The centrepiece is a planned industrial park on its roughly 2,500-acre Lembah Beringin landbank, with the first phase targeted for FY2027 and revenue recognition expected from FY2028, alongside a RM500 million stratified industrial and commercial project on 13.74 acres in Tampoi, Johor.

KEB Inks IPO Underwriting Deal

Property developer KEB Berhad has signed an underwriting agreement with M & A Securities Sdn Bhd ahead of its planned listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia.
M & A Securities will underwrite 66.18 million new shares, comprising 44.12 million shares for the Malaysian public and 22.06 million shares for eligible directors, employees and contributors to the Group.
The IPO involves a public issue of 138.54 million new shares and an offer for sale of 88.24 million existing shares, totalling 226.78 million shares. The remaining shares will be placed privately with MITI-approved Bumiputera investors and selected investors.
Proceeds from the public issue will go towards landbank acquisition, project working capital, repayment of bank borrowings and listing expenses.
Founded in 2004, KEB has completed 14 projects and has two ongoing developments worth RM773.29 million in gross development value (GDV), with four future projects valued at RM940.74 million. Its construction arm, KEB Utama Sdn Bhd, is a CIDB Grade G7 contractor.
M & A Securities is the principal adviser, sponsor, placement agent and underwriter, while Eco Asia Capital Advisory Sdn Bhd is the financial adviser.

CARSOME Academy Marks Fifth Year

CARSOME Academy has marked its fifth anniversary with more than RM2 million in funding and scholarships to train Malaysians for automotive careers.
This includes the RM1.65 million Accelerate with TVET Programme, anchored by Maybank Islamic Berhad, and more than RM350,000 in Selangor State Government scholarships for Asnaf and B40 students.
The Academy has also signed an MoU with JETOUR Automobile Malaysia to offer work placements, and launched two automotive sales TVET programmes with SKM certification.
Since 2021, 593 students have registered with the Academy, with 90% finding jobs within three months.

Aneka Jaringan Wins RM26.2m Contract

Basement and foundation specialist Aneka Jaringan Holdings Berhad has secured a RM26.20 million contract for a high-rise serviced apartment project in Kuala Lumpur.
Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Aneka Jaringan Sdn Bhd, accepted the Letter of Award from WDA Architects Sdn Bhd on behalf of Exsim YKS 54 Sdn Bhd. The job covers earthworks, piling and pile caps, retaining wall and substructure works for a 53-storey, 394-unit serviced apartment development on Jalan Yap Kwan Seng.
The contract began on 15 September 2026 and is due for completion by 14 August 2028. The Group said it is expected to contribute positively to earnings and net assets for the financial years ending 31 August 2027 and 2028.

DC Healthcare Opens Four Clinics

Medical aesthetic services provider DC Healthcare Holdings Berhad has opened four new clinics across Johor, Selangor and Penang between July and September 2026.
Three are under its Dr Chong Clinic brand, in Muar, USJ Taipan and Setia Alam, while the Penang Greenlane outlet marks the launch of a new brand, DC Plus Clinic.
The expansion comes as the Group’s core aesthetic services segment grows, with revenue rising 15% year-on-year to RM20.44 million in Q2 FY2026, and 20% to RM39.12 million for the first half.

EcoSys Launches IPO Prospectus

Industrial solutions provider EcoSys (Malaysia) Berhad has launched its prospectus for an initial public offering on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia, aiming to raise RM39.34 million.
The IPO involves a public issue of 145.70 million new shares at RM0.27 each, representing about 25.5% of the company’s enlarged share capital of 571.35 million shares. There is no offer for sale.
EcoSys serves the pan-semiconductor industry through ultra-high purity fabrication of precision engineering components and the development and maintenance of abatement systems.
Most of the proceeds, RM17 million, will go towards expanding its abatement segment, with RM8 million for repaying bank borrowings and RM4.93 million for new machinery and staff. A further RM1.54 million will fund a sales and service centre in India, which accounted for RM38.22 million, or 35.1%, of the Group’s revenue in FYE2025.
M & A Securities Sdn Bhd is the Principal Adviser, Sponsor, Underwriter and Placement Agent, while Eco Asia Capital Advisory Sdn Bhd is the Financial Adviser.

title: CARSOME Academy Marks 5 Years with more than RM2 Million in Support to Build Malaysia’s Automotive Talent
body: Selangor State Government to continue supporting CARSOME Academy with more than RM350,000 in scholarships for Asnaf and B40 students Partnerships with Maybank Islamic Berhad and JETOUR Automobile Malaysia connect automotive training with industry experience and employment opportunities The Academy launches two new TVET programmes, the first known industry-led programmes of their kind in Malaysia, combining automotive sales expertise with nationally recognised SKM certification  Kuala Lumpur, 24 September 2026 – CARSOME Academy marked its fifth anniversary with more than RM2 million in combined financial support, scholarships and development funding, alongside new partnerships and programmes aimed at preparing Malaysians for careers across the automotive industry.  The milestone brings together support from the Selangor State Government, Maybank Islamic Berhad and industry partner JETOUR Automobile Malaysia, expanding opportunities for Malaysians to gain industry-relevant skills, practical experiences, and access to careers in the automotive industry.  The RM1.65 million Accelerate with TVET Programme, anchored by Maybank Islamic Berhad, alongside matching contributions from Bank Negara Malaysia, CARSOME Academy and Etiqa General Takaful, will provide greater access to industry-relevant technical and vocational education and training.  “TVET is a powerful pathway to equip Malaysians with the practical skills and opportunities they need for the future. To us, Maybank’s Humanising Financial Services means creating opportunities that make a meaningful difference to people and communities. We are proud to partner with CARSOME Academy to expand access to industry-relevant training and strengthen pathways from education to employment. By investing in skills and talent development, we can help build a more inclusive, capable and future-ready workforce, while contributing to a positive and lasting impact for Malaysian society,” said Mohamad Yasin Abdullah, CEO, Maybank Islamic Berhad.  CARSOME Academy and Maybank Islamic Berhad mark their partnership with an MoU, supporting scholarships and greater access to automotive TVET education for aspiring talent. From L-R: ● Eric Cheng, Co-Founder & Group Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME ● Teoh Jiun Ee, CARSOME Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy ● Mohamad Yasin Abdullah, CEO, Maybank Islamic Berhad ● Nur Hidayah Salim, Head, Group Values-Based Centre of Excellence  This is further supported by more than RM350,000 in scholarships from the Selangor State Government through IKTISASS and Yayasan MBI, benefiting Asnaf and B40 students from Selangor.  Speaking at the Academy’s fifth anniversary celebration, Yang Berhormat Tuan Mohd Najwan Bin Halimi, Selangor State Exco for Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship, said the Selangor Government would continue to support CARSOME Academy as a homegrown company contributing to the state’s automotive talent and economic development.  Y.B. Tuan Mohd Najwan bin Halimi, Selangor State Exco for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship, delivers his speech at CARSOME Academy’s 5th anniversary celebration and graduation ceremony.  “Selangor will continue to stand with CARSOME Academy. As a company that was born in Selangor, headquartered in Petaling Jaya and committed to training young people in the automotive sector, CARSOME Academy is an important partner in developing the talent that contributes to our state’s economy. The Selangor State Government looks forward to expanding this collaboration,” he said.  CARSOME Group is also contributing an additional RM150,000 towards scholarships, with other funding and development commitments bringing the Academy’s total support to more than RM2 million.  JETOUR Partnership Expands Industry Pathways  Complementing the TVET initiative, CARSOME Academy has signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with JETOUR Automobile Malaysia to create work placement and practical job opportunities for its students and graduates across various areas of the industry, including vehicle inspection, sales, and aftersales.  Through the partnership, CARSOME Academy and JETOUR will work together to structure and develop trainee programmes that give learners hands-on industry experience and opportunities to build their technical skills in real-world automotive settings.  CARSOME Academy and JETOUR Automobile Malaysia formalise their partnership through an MoU to connect automotive TVET training with industry exposure and employment opportunities. From L-R: ● Eric Cheng, Co-Founder & Group Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME ● Teoh Jiun Ee, CARSOME Co-Founder & Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy ● Nicholas Ng, Vice President, Jetour Malaysia ● Mohd Azhar, Sales Director, Jetour Malaysia  “Industry exposure is essential in preparing the next generation of automotive talent. As the automotive industry continues to evolve, stronger collaboration between industry and TVET institutions play our part in bridging the gap between education and industry, while providing students with meaningful opportunities to gain real-world experience and insights into the automotive industry,” said Nicholas Ng, Vice President of Jetour Malaysia.  Five Years of Impact and The Road Ahead  Since 2021, 593 students have registered with CARSOME Academy, with 90% securing employment within three months. The Academy has also trained more than 8,000 employees, developed more than 500 leaders and supported 280 scholarship recipients.  Building on this foundation, the Academy is growing its role across the automotive ecosystem through five key pillars spanning vehicle inspection, TVET, corporate training, talent and job matching, and industry partnerships.  This includes two new automotive sales TVET programmes, Certified Sales Professional and Certified Sales Excellence, the first known industry-led TVET programmes of their kind in Malaysia, combining practical automotive sales expertise with nationally recognised SKM certification.  “Five years on, the impact of CARSOME Academy is clear, from building technical capabilities to creating real opportunities for employment. With 593 students trained and 90% securing employment within three months, we have seen first hand how industry-led training can translate into a meaningful career,” said Teoh Jiun Ee, Chief Executive Officer of CARSOME Academy and Co-founder of CARSOME Group.
